content.thinking:
I'm drafting the postmortem now, noting the memory leak caused latency degradation but error rates stayed flat, meaning users only felt the slowdown, not failures. The restart resolved the symptom, but the root cause remains unidentified since no deploy or config change was found and the code-fix analysis ran out of budget before pinpointing the leak source.

I'll describe the incident window and duration qualitatively rather than restating given figures as if I computed them myself. I'll flag key assumptions clearly: that the same leak is likely to recur, that the latency issue stems from GC pressure though this wasn't directly confirmed, and that the baseline disconnect errors are unrelated background noise.

assumptions: The leak is assumed to be internal to io-shop: no deploy, release, config change or flag toggle was recorded in the windows searched, so nothing external was confirmed as a trigger — absence of a recorded change is not proof no change occurred.
The latency degradation is attributed to GC pressure from the growing heap; this was inferred from the correlation between heap growth and rising p50/p99, not from GC or profiling data.
The ongoing 'ClientDisconnected' errors on the account page are assumed to be unrelated background noise, since they ran at the same rate for hours before onset and did not rise during the incident.
The service is assumed to have been healthy after the restart because it returned to baseline metrics; the leak itself was not verified as gone, only its accumulated effect cleared.
Because the leak's source was never identified, recurrence is assumed rather than ruled out — no fix was proposed (the code-fix step ran out of budget before submitting one).
input.executive_summary: On the night of 22 September the online shop's service began holding on to memory it should have released. Starting at about 23:18 UTC the service got progressively slower for shoppers — pages that normally returned in a fraction of a second took several times longer as the problem grew — until it was restarted and returned to normal at 23:44 UTC, a window of roughly 26 minutes. Requests kept being served throughout: the share of failing requests stayed at its normal background level and did not rise during the event, so the shopper-visible impact was slowness rather than outright errors. Automated on-call detected the problem, reviewed metrics, recent production changes and logs, and restarted the service, which brought it back to its baseline within about a minute of acting. The restart cleared the symptom only; the underlying cause of the memory growth has not been found or fixed, and an attempt to propose a code fix did not complete, so the condition can be expected to return.
input.root_cause: io-shop leaked memory in-process: its heap grew monotonically (~460MB to ~1.38GB, still climbing at alert time against a 2048MiB limit) from roughly 23:14-23:18 while request volume stayed flat and the process was never restarted, and the resulting GC pressure degraded latency (p50 ~45→147ms, p99 ~375→1231ms). No deploy, config change or feature-flag toggle was found in any window searched (up to ~8 days back), so the specific leaking allocation was never identified — the diagnosis is an unreleased allocation inferred from the heap and latency shape, not a located code defect.
